newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Mahogany may soon join list of endangered species.
newsitem.headline: Mahogany may soon join list of endangered species.

text.p: A leading environmental pressure group Greenpeace said on Monday there was a good chance that bigleaf mahogany, found mostly on the American continent, would be listed as an endangered species at a world conference in Zimbabwe.

Isabel McCrea, a spokeswoman for the Amsterdam-based group, said a proposal by Bolivia and the United States to a 10-day Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) would help control trade in bigleaf mahogany.
Bolivia is the world's largest mahogany exporter and the U.S., the largest importer.
The proposal is one of about 80, including a controversial one calling for a partial lifting of the ban on ivory trading, to be submitted to the 138-member convention for consideration.

"Many scientists agree that mahogany is currently being logged at unsustainable rates and that a large proportion of wood exported is being done in violation of national laws," McCrea said, pointing to a recent audit by Brazil indicating gross irregularities.
She said the chances of listing mahogany under Appendix II of CITES were good, although CITES members were facing a lot of pressure from the timber industry.
Appendix II allows limited trade in endangererd species.
"In the five years since the first proposal to list mahogany at CITES, fears that the species may be heading toward commercial extinction have grown," she said.
